biggest_catch: A general training session is mandatory for most elections, but no training pay or duration is published.
catches: Full-day election officer pay is $200; half-day shift (5:00 AM-1:00 PM or 12:30 PM until finished) is $80.
Officers must be at the polls from 5:00 AM until polls close, results are called in, and all forms/equipment are complete (usually 8:00-9:00 PM).
A general training session for most elections is mandatory, but the county publishes no training pay or duration.
Officers may also serve as unpaid volunteers; this route uses the $200 full-day paid option.
Must be a United States citizen and registered to vote in Virginia; cannot hold any elected office.

steps: Confirm eligibility: United States citizen and registered voter in Virginia, not holding elected office.
Sign up with the Loudoun County Office of Elections and Voter Registration.
Attend the mandatory general training session (most elections).
Work a full Election Day (5:00 AM until results are called in and equipment stowed, usually 8:00-9:00 PM).
timing: Election Day 5:00 AM until finished (usually 8:00-9:00 PM), approximately 15-16 hours.
weasel_words: Mandatory training is required but its duration and pay are not published, so no training time or pay is counted.
Half-day shifts ($80) are a separate mechanism not used in this route.
Officers may waive pay and serve as volunteers; this route uses the paid full-day option.
